rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 (wide array x = -0.04 to +0.04, sensor_size 0.012, kp 3.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6) scored 52.97. It is slightly below iteration 1's 55.46, and all 60 trials still went off track. Line-loss events fell from about 2 to 1, but max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m, just over the 0.06 m limit. Widening the array did not stop the drift, so sensor coverage is not the main limit.

The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). With body_width up to 0.18 the limit only reaches 0.0575, so the 0.06 m floor binds and body width cannot relax it. The robot must stay within 0.06 m of the centre line.

My hypothesis is that the sensors sit only 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line too late. At 1.6 base_speed the robot covers the bend before the correction takes effect, and the error peaks just past 0.06 m. Moving the sensor row forward to y = 0.07 m gives more lookahead, so the correction starts earlier and the overshoot should shrink.

Changes: (1) move all five sensors from y = 0.04 to y = 0.07 m, keeping the wide x spacing (-0.04 to +0.04), sensor_size 0.012 and weights unchanged; (2) keep kp 3.5 and kd 0.3 unchanged, since the signal scale is the same and the geometry is the only major change; (3) keep base_speed 1.6 and line_loss last_direction so that this is a single-variable test of lookahead.

Expected result: max_error drops below 0.06 m, line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1, and progress rises above 0.2 on the s-bend and slalom. Risks: the signal may react more to early curvature, so steering_oscillation could rise. If max_error still exceeds 0.06 m with line loss at 0 or 1, the next step is a higher kd to damp overshoot. If line loss stays near 1 to 2, test line_loss search_left or search_right. If the robot stays on track but does not finish, raise base_speed toward 2.0.
